title: Infrastructure: Tool execution timeout and async support
description:
Basic timeout infrastructure for new tools.

## Scope (simplified from original)
Focus on basic timeout support first. Async job execution deferred to separate issue.

## Problem scenarios
- search_content on huge repo: could take minutes
- fetch_url on slow server: could hang
- project_files with deep recursion: could be slow

## Implementation

### 1. Universal timeout wrapper
```elisp
(defun efrit-with-tool-timeout (timeout-secs body-fn)
  "Execute BODY-FN with TIMEOUT-SECS limit.
Returns result or timeout error in standard format."
  (with-timeout (timeout-secs 
                 '((success . nil) 
                   (error . ((type . "timeout")
                            (message . "Tool execution timed out")))))
    (funcall body-fn)))
```

### 2. Per-tool timeout configuration
```elisp
(defcustom efrit-tool-timeouts
  '((search_content . 60)
    (project_files . 30)
    (fetch_url . 30)
    (vcs_blame . 45)
    (default . 30))
  "Timeout in seconds for each tool.")
```

### 3. Progress reporting (optional enhancement)
- Long-running tools can emit progress via efrit-progress.el
- Not required for MVP, but nice to have

## Deferred to separate issue
- Async job execution (tool returns job ID, check later)
- This is complex and not needed for Phase 1

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All new tools wrapped in timeout
- [ ] Timeout produces standard error response
- [ ] Timeouts are configurable
- [ ] Tests verify timeout behavior

title: Implement search_content tool
description:
Grep-like content search across the codebase.

## Input schema
- pattern: search pattern (string)
- is_regex: whether pattern is regex (default: false for literal search)
- path: search scope (default: project root)
- file_pattern: glob filter for files to search (e.g., '*.el', '*.py')
- context_lines: lines before/after match (default: 2)
- max_results: limit results (default: 50)
- case_sensitive: (default: false)
- offset: for pagination (default: 0)

## Output (following standard format)
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "matches": [
      {
        "file": "/absolute/path/to/file.el",
        "file_relative": "lisp/file.el",
        "line": 42,
        "column": 15,
        "content": "the matching line content",
        "context_before": ["line 40", "line 41"],
        "context_after": ["line 43", "line 44"]
      }
    ],
    "truncated": true,
    "total_matches": 150,
    "returned": 50,
    "files_searched": 234,
    "continuation_hint": "Use offset=50 to get more"
  }
}
```

## Implementation priority
1. ripgrep (rg) - fastest, best regex support
2. grep - widely available fallback
3. Elisp-native - last resort, slowest

### ripgrep command
```bash
rg --json --max-count=<max_results> \\
   --context=<context_lines> \\
   --glob='<file_pattern>' \\
   '<pattern>' '<path>'
```

## Edge cases
- Binary files: skip by default (rg does this)
- Very long lines: truncate at 500 chars
- Multi-line matches: include full match with \\n preserved
- Empty results: return empty matches array, not error
- Pattern with special chars: proper escaping based on is_regex

## Performance
- Timeout: 60 seconds (configurable)
- Early termination when max_results reached
- Stream results if possible (don't buffer entire output)

## Depends on
- ef-9hc: Security model (sandbox checks)
- ef-05m: Timeout infrastructure
- ef-ej7: Path/error standards

title: DRY up tool handler boilerplate with macro/helper
description:

```elisp
(defun efrit-do--handle-FOO (tool-input)

      (efrit-do--validate-required tool-input "foo" "field1")
      (let* ((args (efrit-do--extract-fields tool-input '("field1" "field2")))
             (result (efrit-tool-foo args)))

```

```elisp
    (fn-name tool-name required-fields field-specs underlying-fn label &optional require-lib)
  ...)
```

Then replace boilerplate handlers with one-liners.

title: Implement elisp_docs tool
description:
Structured Emacs Lisp documentation lookup.

## Input schema
- symbol: function, variable, or face name
- type: 'function' | 'variable' | 'face' | 'auto' (default: auto)
- include_source: whether to include source location (default: false)
- related: whether to include related symbols via apropos (default: false)

## Output
- found: boolean
- type: what kind of symbol it is
- docstring: the documentation
- signature: for functions, the argument list
- source_file: where it's defined
- source_line: line number in source
- related_symbols: if requested, similar names from apropos

## Implementation
Use Emacs' built-in documentation system:
- describe-function, describe-variable, describe-face
- find-function-noselect for source location
- apropos for related symbols

## Why better than (describe-function ...)
- Structured output Claude can reliably parse
- Doesn't open help buffer (side effect free)
- Can batch multiple lookups
- Includes source location for deeper investigation

## No security concerns
Purely local, read-only access to Emacs' own documentation.

title: Agent input starts efrit-do session when no session active
description:
Modify `efrit-agent-input-send` to start a new efrit-do async session when the user presses RET in the agent buffer and no session is currently active.

This is the core REPL behavior: type a command at the `> ` prompt, hit RET, and a session starts.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. With no active session, typing at `> ` prompt and pressing RET starts a new session
2. The session is identical to one started via `M-x efrit-do` (same behavior, same progress buffer)
3. Agent buffer header-line changes from "Idle" to "Working"
4. User message appears in conversation region with `> ` prefix
5. Claude responses stream into the conversation region above
6. With an active session, input continues to work as before (guidance injection, question responses)
7. `make compile` passes
design:
## What to Build

Extend `efrit-agent-input-send` in `efrit-agent-input.el` to detect when no session is active and start a new one.

## Implementation

Modify `efrit-agent-input-send` in `lisp/interfaces/efrit-agent-input.el`:

```elisp
(defun efrit-agent-input-send ()
  "Send the current input."
  (interactive)
  (let ((input (efrit-agent--get-input)))
    (if (or (null input) (string-empty-p (string-trim input)))
        (message "Nothing to send")
      ;; Add to history and show in conversation
      (efrit-agent--add-to-history input)
      (efrit-agent--reset-history-navigation)
      (efrit-agent--add-user-message input)
      (efrit-agent--clear-input)
      (goto-char efrit-agent--input-start)
      
      (let ((session (efrit-session-active)))
        (cond
         ;; Existing: respond or inject guidance to active session
         (session
          (if (efrit-session-waiting-for-user-p session)
              (progn
                (efrit-session-respond-to-question session input)
                (setq efrit-agent--pending-question nil)
                (efrit-agent-set-status 'working))
            (efrit-session-add-message session 'user input)
            (message "Guidance injected to session")))
         
         ;; NEW: start a new efrit-do session from this input
         (t
          (require 'efrit-do)
          (let ((session (efrit-do--start-async-session input)))
            ;; Attach this buffer's UI state to the new session
            (setq efrit-agent--session-id (efrit-session-id session))
            (setq efrit-agent--command input)
            (setq efrit-agent--status 'working)
            (setq efrit-agent--start-time (current-time))
            ;; Initialize pending tools hash table
            (setq efrit-agent--pending-tools (make-hash-table :test 'equal))
            ;; Start elapsed timer if not running
            (unless efrit-agent--elapsed-timer
              (setq efrit-agent--elapsed-timer
                    (run-at-time 1 1 #'efrit-agent--update-elapsed (current-buffer))))
            (message "Efrit: started session from agent buffer"))))))))
```

Also add a forward declaration near the top of the file:
```elisp
(declare-function efrit-do--start-async-session "efrit-do")
```

## Files to Modify
- `lisp/interfaces/efrit-agent-input.el`

## Verification Steps
1. `M-x efrit-agent-open`
2. Type a command at `> ` prompt and press RET
3. User message appears in conversation with `> ` prefix
4. Header-line changes to "Working" with elapsed time
5. Progress buffer appears (same as efrit-do behavior)
6. Claude responses stream into agent buffer above the input region
7. After completion, header-line shows "Complete"
8. With a session running, typing at prompt injects guidance (existing behavior preserved)
9. `make compile` passes

title: Epic: Smart output management mode for agent buffer
description:
Transform the agent buffer from a linear log display into a sophisticated output management interface that shows collapsed summaries by default with intelligent expansion and type-specific rendering.

This is our primary ergonomic differentiator vs. web-based coding assistants. Modern tools (Amp, Claude Code) suppress output, show snippets, and provide expandable details. Emacs can do this *better* with proper mode design.

Goals:
- Keep agent buffer scannable and clean (collapsed by default)
- Provide click-to-expand access to full tool output
- Type-aware rendering (diffs, JSON, code, grep results, etc.)
- Context-sensitive summaries (e.g., "3 files modified, click to expand")
- Error emphasis (auto-expand failures, collapse successes)
- Remember expansion state across re-renders
- Support copy/navigation/interaction with rendered content

This epic is intentionally self-expanding. Start with design phase to create detailed implementation tasks.

title: Implement project_files tool
description:
Give Claude visibility into project file structure.

## Input schema
- path: directory to scan (default: project root via project.el)
- pattern: glob pattern filter (optional, e.g., '*.el')
- max_depth: recursion depth (default: 5, 0 = current dir only)
- include_hidden: include dotfiles/dotdirs (default: false)
- max_files: limit total files returned (default: 500)
- offset: for pagination (default: 0)

## Output (following standard format)
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "root": "/absolute/path/to/project",
    "project_type": "git",
    "files": [
      {
        "path": "/absolute/path/to/file.el",
        "path_relative": "lisp/file.el",
        "size": 12345,
        "mtime": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
        "is_directory": false,
        "is_symlink": false
      }
    ],
    "directories": 45,
    "total_files": 234,
    "truncated": false,
    "gitignore_respected": true
  }
}
```

## Implementation notes
- Use project.el for root detection (project-current, project-root)
- Use directory-files-recursively for traversal
- Respect .gitignore if git project (use git ls-files when possible)
- Format timestamps as ISO 8601

## Output format options
Two modes (controlled by 'format' parameter):
1. 'flat' (default): Simple list of files as shown above
2. 'tree': Nested structure mirroring directory hierarchy

## Edge cases
- Symlinks: include but mark is_symlink=true, don't follow
- Permission denied: skip file, include in warnings
- Very deep nesting: respect max_depth strictly
- No project detected: use current directory as root, warn

## Project type detection
Check for (in order):
- .git → 'git'
- package.json → 'npm'  
- Cargo.toml → 'cargo'
- setup.py/pyproject.toml → 'python'
- Makefile → 'make'
- None → 'unknown'

## Performance
- Timeout: 30 seconds
- Use git ls-files when possible (much faster for git repos)
- Consider caching project structure (invalidate on file changes)

## Depends on
- ef-9hc: Security model (sandbox)
- ef-ej7: Path/error standards

## Comprehensive Agent REPL Testing Plan

Thorough manual testing of the Efrit agent REPL interface to verify:
- Command input/output flow
- Streaming response handling
- Error handling and recovery
- Multi-turn conversations
- Tool execution and result display
- Buffer state management
- Async operations

### Setup
1. Start fresh Emacs: `emacs -Q`
2. Load efrit config: Add to init.el or eval manually
3. Open agent: `M-x efrit-agent`

### Test 1: Basic REPL Interaction
**Objective**: Verify simple command input/output works

1. Type in agent buffer: `hello, what is 2+2?`
2. Press RET, wait for response stream
3. Expected:
   - Response appears in buffer
   - No errors in *Messages*
   - Prompt `> ` reappears when done
   - Response is readable/formatted

### Test 2: Multi-turn Conversation
**Objective**: Verify session context is maintained

1. In agent, type: `my name is alice`
2. Wait for completion
3. Type: `what did i just tell you?`
4. Wait for response
5. Expected:
   - Claude remembers "alice" from previous turn
   - Conversation flows naturally
   - No duplicate messages
   - Buffer doesn't scroll unexpectedly

### Test 3: Tool Execution Flow
**Objective**: Verify tools execute and display correctly

1. Type: `please evaluate this: (+ 10 20 30)`
2. Wait for response
3. Expected:
   - eval_sexp tool executes
   - Result (60) appears in response
   - Tool call is visible in buffer (if auto-expand enabled)
   - No "Wrong type argument" errors

### Test 4: File Operations
**Objective**: Verify file tool execution in REPL

1. Type: `create a test file /tmp/test-efrit.txt with content "hello world"`
2. Wait for completion
3. Verify file exists: `cat /tmp/test-efrit.txt`
4. Type in agent: `read /tmp/test-efrit.txt for me`
5. Expected:
   - File is created
   - File read tool executes
   - Content displays in response
   - No permission errors

### Test 5: Error Recovery
**Objective**: Verify REPL recovers from errors

1. Type: `evaluate this broken code: (list 1 2 3` (missing paren)
2. Wait for response
3. Type: `now evaluate this working code: (+ 1 1)`
4. Expected:
   - First command shows syntax error gracefully
   - Second command works fine
   - No cascading errors
   - Prompt remains responsive
   - Buffer state isn't corrupted

### Test 6: Streaming Large Responses
**Objective**: Verify streaming works for large outputs

1. Type: `generate a list of 20 numbers and their squares`
2. Watch response stream in
3. Expected:
   - Text appears progressively
   - Buffer scrolls smoothly
   - No freezing/blocking
   - Complete response arrives
   - No truncation/missing content

### Test 7: Long-running Operations
**Objective**: Verify user can interact during async operations

1. Type: `evaluate (sleep-for 2)` (or similar long operation)
2. WHILE it's running, try typing more input
3. Wait for first to complete
4. Expected:
   - Operation runs without blocking UI
   - New input queues properly
   - Commands execute in order
   - No lost input

### Test 8: Buffer State Consistency
**Objective**: Verify buffer doesn't get corrupted

1. Run 5+ commands in sequence
2. Scroll through buffer
3. Kill buffer: `C-x k` on agent buffer
4. Reopen: `M-x efrit-agent`
5. Type new command
6. Expected:
   - Scrolling works smoothly
   - No overlapping text
   - Kill/reopen works
   - New session starts cleanly
   - No leftover state issues

### Test 9: Copy/Paste in REPL
**Objective**: Verify clipboard operations work

1. Copy some text to clipboard
2. In agent prompt, paste: `C-y`
3. Add to it, press RET
4. Expected:
   - Paste inserts correctly
   - Command executes
   - Response appears

### Test 10: Special Characters and Multiline
**Objective**: Verify handling of complex input

1. Copy this to clipboard and paste in agent:
   ```
   create a function that takes two numbers and returns their sum.
   also explain how it works
   ```
2. Press RET (might need C-u C-j for multiline entry)
3. Expected:
   - Multiline input handled correctly
   - Claude understands full request
   - Response is appropriate
   - No parsing errors

### Test 11: Tool Result Formatting
**Objective**: Verify tools display results nicely

1. Type: `show me the directory listing of /tmp` (shell_exec)
2. Type: `evaluate (user-full-name)` (eval_sexp)
3. Type: `what is the emacs version?` (should detect and respond)
4. Expected:
   - Shell output formatted readably
   - Code evaluation result clear
   - Mixed responses coherent
   - No raw JSON/internal formats visible

### Test 12: Session Management
**Objective**: Verify session tracking works

1. Run `M-x efrit-session-list` (if available)
2. Note active session ID
3. Run several commands in agent
4. Check session transcript/history
5. Expected:
   - Session tracked
   - All commands recorded
   - Responses logged
   - Metrics tracked (tokens, etc)
   - Can view history

### Test 13: Interruption Handling
**Objective**: Verify user can interrupt/cancel

1. Start a long command
2. While streaming, press `C-c` (if interrupt supported)
3. Type a new command
4. Expected:
   - Can interrupt gracefully
   - New command starts
   - Or: interrupt not supported but doesn't crash

### Test 14: Buffer Navigation
**Objective**: Verify movement through responses

1. Run 3-4 commands with substantial responses
2. Use `M-p` / `M-n` (or `C-p` / `C-n`) to navigate history
3. Edit a previous command, re-send
4. Expected:
   - Command history navigation works

   - Response appears

### Test 15: No Memory Leaks
**Objective**: Verify long sessions don't degrade

1. Run 20+ commands in sequence (can use script)
2. Monitor Emacs memory usage
3. Check for slowdown in response times
4. Expected:
   - No significant slowdown after many commands
   - Memory usage reasonable
   - Buffer remains responsive
   - Final commands execute as quickly as first

## Test Execution

- [ ] Document any failures with exact steps, expected vs actual
- [ ] Note any warnings in *Messages* or logs
- [ ] File bugs for any issues found using:

title: Identical tool call detection not catching glob_files loops
description:
The circuit breaker's identical-call detection (efrit-do-max-identical-tool-calls=3) is not stopping glob_files loops effectively.

**Evidence from multiple dogfood tests:**

Test 1: 'List all the .el files in /Users/stevey/src/efrit/lisp/core/ and count how many there are'
- 13 glob_files calls with same input hash before circuit breaker stopped it

Test 2: 'Create a new buffer called *dogfood-test* with a list of all .el files in /Users/stevey/src/efrit/lisp/'  
- 11 consecutive glob_files calls
- Circuit breaker never tripped
- Session had to be manually cancelled

**Root cause analysis:**
1. The identical call counter appears to be reset between API continuations
2. Each new continuation starts fresh, so 'identical' count never reaches 3 within a single API call
3. The circuit breaker only checks within a single response, not across the session

**Real impact:**
- Simple file listing tasks burn 10-13x more tokens than needed
- glob_files tool appears broken - Claude keeps retrying it
- May also indicate glob_files is returning an error that makes Claude retry

**Fix needed:**
1. Persist identical-call counters across continuations
2. OR: Track tool call patterns at the session level, not response level
3. Investigate why glob_files results make Claude want to retry

design:
## What to Build

A new command `efrit-agent-open` in `lisp/interfaces/efrit-agent.el` that:
1. Gets or creates the `*efrit-agent*` buffer
2. Initializes `efrit-agent-mode` if not already active
3. Sets up conversation/input regions if needed
4. Sets status to 'idle when no session exists
5. Displays buffer at bottom and moves point to input region

## Implementation

Add this function to `efrit-agent.el`:

```elisp
;;;###autoload
(defun efrit-agent-open ()
  "Open or switch to the Efrit agent buffer in idle mode.
Provides a persistent prompt buffer for interacting with Efrit.
Type at the > prompt to start a session (once Task 2 is done)."
  (interactive)
  (let ((buffer (efrit-agent--get-buffer)))
    (with-current-buffer buffer
      ;; Initialize mode if not already done
      (unless (derived-mode-p 'efrit-agent-mode)
        (efrit-agent-mode))
      ;; Initialize regions if not set up
      (unless (and efrit-agent--conversation-end
                   (marker-position efrit-agent--conversation-end))
        (efrit-agent--init-regions)
        (efrit-agent--setup-regions))
      ;; Set idle state if no active session
      (unless efrit-agent--session-id
        (setq efrit-agent--status 'idle)
        (setq efrit-agent--start-time nil)))
    ;; Display and focus
    (display-buffer buffer '(display-buffer-at-bottom (window-height . 15)))
    (select-window (get-buffer-window buffer))
    (goto-char (point-max))))
```

## Files to Modify
- `lisp/interfaces/efrit-agent.el` - Add the new command

## Verification Steps
1. Run `M-x efrit-agent-open`
2. Verify buffer `*efrit-agent*` opens at bottom
3. Header-line shows "○ Idle"
4. Conversation region (above separator) is read-only

title: Potential timer leak in file watcher callbacks (efrit-remote-queue.el)
description:
In efrit-remote-queue.el line 526, each file system event creates a fire-and-forget timer with run-at-time. Under heavy file I/O or rapid file writes, this could accumulate timer objects that are never tracked or explicitly canceled.

The timer pattern:
```
(run-at-time 0.1 nil #'efrit-remote-queue--process-file file-path)
```

This is a one-shot timer (interval=nil), but:
1. Not tracked in any hash table or variable
2. Called from a file watcher callback that fires on every file event
3. Could accumulate hundreds of timers if files are written rapidly

Potential solutions:
1. Add a debounce mechanism to prevent multiple timers for the same file
2. Use a timer tracking hash table like async-loop uses
3. Add a maximum pending timers guard

Note: Low risk since each timer is one-shot, but could affect performance under heavy load.
acceptance_criteria: When file watcher is under heavy load (100+ files written quickly), verify that pending timers don't accumulate beyond a reasonable threshold (max ~20-30 pending).

description:
Read arbitrary files, not just open buffers.

## Input schema
- path: file to read (absolute or project-relative)
- start_line: optional line to start from (1-indexed)
- end_line: optional line to end at (inclusive)
- encoding: optional encoding override (default: auto-detect)
- max_size: max bytes to read (default: 100000, ~100KB)

## Output (following standard format)
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "path": "/absolute/path/to/file.el",
    "path_relative": "lisp/file.el",
    "content": "file contents here...",
    "encoding": "utf-8",
    "size": 12345,
    "mtime": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
    "total_lines": 500,
    "lines_returned": "1-500",
    "truncated": false
  },
  "warnings": []
}
```

## Large file handling
- Files > max_size: truncate and set truncated=true
- Include message: "File truncated at 100KB. Use start_line/end_line for specific sections."
- If start_line/end_line specified, read only that range (more efficient)

## Binary file handling
- Detect binary via: null bytes in first 8KB, or known binary extensions
- For binary files, return:
  ```json
  {
    "success": true,
    "result": {
      "path": "...",
      "is_binary": true,
      "size": 50000,
      "mime_type": "image/png",
      "content": null
    },
    "warnings": ["Binary file detected, content not returned"]
  }
  ```
- Do NOT base64 encode (too large for context)

## Encoding handling
1. Check for encoding cookie (e.g., -*- coding: utf-8 -*-)
2. Check BOM
3. Try utf-8
4. Fall back to system locale
5. If all fail, try latin-1 (accepts anything)

## Security
- Sandbox check via efrit-resolve-path
- Sensitive file check against blocklist
- If sensitive file requested: require confirmation or error

## Difference from eval_sexp + find-file
- read_file is read-only (safer)
- Doesn't create buffers (lighter weight)
- Structured output with metadata
- Binary detection
- Line range support

title: Epic: Conversational Efrit - Progress Visibility and User Interaction
Infrastructure: Standardize tool path handling and error responses
description:
Define consistent conventions for all new tools.

## Problem
Current tool designs have inconsistent approaches to:
- Path input (absolute? relative? project-relative?)
- Error responses (format, structure)
- Large result handling (truncation, pagination)

## Path Handling Standard

### Input paths
- All tools accept both absolute and project-relative paths
- Project-relative paths resolved via efrit-resolve-path helper
- Empty/nil path defaults to project root (detected via project.el)
- Paths outside project root: error if sandboxed, warn if not

### Helper function
```elisp
(defun efrit-resolve-path (path &optional allow-outside)
  "Resolve PATH relative to project root.
If PATH is absolute, use as-is (with sandbox check).
If PATH is relative, resolve against project root.
If ALLOW-OUTSIDE is nil and path escapes sandbox, signal error."
  ...)
```

### Path in output
- Always return absolute paths in output
- Include project-relative version for display

## Error Response Standard

All tools should return consistent error format:
```json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "not_found" | "permission_denied" | "timeout" | "invalid_input" | ...,
    "message": "Human-readable error message",
    "details": { ... optional structured details ... }
  }
}
```

Success responses:
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "result": { ... tool-specific result ... },
  "warnings": [ ... optional warnings ... ]
}
```

## Large Result Standard

For tools that can return large results (project_files, search_content, etc.):

### Truncation
- Default max_results or max_size per tool
- Always include truncation indicator:
  ```json
  {
    "truncated": true,
    "total_available": 1500,
    "returned": 50,
    "continuation_hint": "Use offset=50 to get more"
  }
  ```

### Pagination pattern
- All list-returning tools support: offset, limit
- Default limit is tool-specific but reasonable (50-100)

## Implementation
- Create efrit-tool-utils.el with helpers
- Update all tool handlers to use standard patterns
- Document in tool schema descriptions

## Must complete before
Any Phase 1 tool implementation

title: Implement web_search tool
description:
Search the web for documentation, solutions, examples.

## Input schema
- query: search terms (required)
- site: site restriction (e.g., 'emacs.stackexchange.com')
- max_results: limit (default: 5)
- type: 'general' | 'docs' | 'code' (default: 'general')

## Output
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "result": {
    "query_used": "emacs parse json elisp",
    "results": [
      {
        "title": "How to parse JSON in Emacs Lisp",
        "url": "https://emacs.stackexchange.com/q/12345",
        "snippet": "You can use json-read-from-string...",
        "source": "emacs.stackexchange.com"
      }
    ],
    "total_estimated": 1500,
    "returned": 5
  }
}
```

## User consent flow

### First use in session
When web_search is called and efrit-enable-web-access is nil:
1. Tool automatically invokes confirm_action:
   - severity: 'info'
   - action: 'Enable web search for this session?'
   - details: ['Query: <the query>', 'This will send the query to <search provider>']
2. If user confirms: set session-local web-access flag, proceed
3. If user rejects: return error with type='permission_denied'

### Subsequent uses
If session already has web-access enabled, proceed without asking.

### Permanent enable
User can set efrit-enable-web-access to t to skip consent.

## Implementation options (choose one)
1. **DuckDuckGo HTML** - No API key, scrape HTML results
   - Pro: Free, no account needed
   - Con: Rate limited, fragile parsing
2. **Brave Search API** - Requires free API key
   - Pro: Good quality, fast, generous free tier
   - Con: Requires signup
3. **SerpAPI** - Requires API key ($)
   - Pro: Reliable, multiple engines
   - Con: Costs money

Recommendation: Start with DuckDuckGo, add Brave as configurable upgrade.

## Rate limiting
- Max 10 searches per session by default
- Configurable via efrit-web-search-max-per-session
- After limit: error with helpful message

## Caching
- Cache results for 1 hour by default
- Same query within cache period returns cached results
- Configurable via efrit-web-search-cache-seconds

## Privacy note
Include in tool description for Claude:
"Note: Search queries are sent to external service. Do not include sensitive user data in queries."

## Depends on
- ef-9hc: Security model (web access controls)
- ef-wv9: confirm_action (for consent flow)

title: glob_files hangs Emacs when called with nil input
description:
When efrit-do--handle-glob-files is called with nil input, it defaults to scanning ~/
recursively for all files. This can hang Emacs for a very long time (or indefinitely) on
systems with large home directories.

**How it happens:**
1. If Claude calls glob_files with malformed input (nil or missing fields)
2. The function defaults: pattern='~/' extension='*' recursive=t  
3. This triggers (directory-files-recursively "~" ".*")
4. On typical systems with large home dirs, this effectively hangs Emacs

**Evidence:**
During dogfooding, the Emacs daemon became unresponsive after glob_files tests.
emacsclient commands timed out until the daemon was killed.

**Fix needed:**
1. Validate inputs more strictly - don't accept nil
2. Limit recursive search depth
3. Use a safer default path like current directory, not ~
4. Add a timeout to file operations

## What to Build

A defcustom flag that, when enabled, hooks efrit-do session starts into the agent buffer.

```elisp
(defcustom efrit-do-use-agent-ui nil
  "When non-nil, show the efrit-agent buffer for efrit-do sessions.

the traditional progress buffer."
  :type 'boolean
  :group 'efrit-do)
```

Modify `efrit-do--start-async-session`:

```elisp
(defun efrit-do--start-async-session (command)
  "Internal helper to start an async efrit-do session for COMMAND."
  ;; Add to history
  (add-to-history 'efrit-do-history command efrit-do-history-max)
  ;; Track command execution
  (efrit-session-track-command command)
  ;; Create session and start async loop
  (let ((session (efrit-do--create-session-for-command command)))

      (let ((buffer (efrit-agent--get-buffer)))
        (with-current-buffer buffer
          (unless (derived-mode-p 'efrit-agent-mode)
            (efrit-agent-mode))
          (efrit-agent--begin-session session command))
        (efrit-agent--show-buffer)))
    
    (efrit-do-async-loop session nil #'efrit-do--on-async-complete)
    session))
```

- `lisp/interfaces/efrit-do.el`

## What to Build

## Implementation

Add to `lisp/interfaces/efrit-agent-core.el` or `efrit-agent.el`:

```elisp
(defun efrit-agent--begin-session (session command)
  "Attach this agent buffer to SESSION for COMMAND.
Resets per-session state but preserves existing conversation text."
  ;; Set new session context
  (setq efrit-agent--session-id (efrit-session-id session))
  (setq efrit-agent--command command)
  (setq efrit-agent--status 'working)
  (setq efrit-agent--start-time (current-time))
  ;; Reset per-session state
  (setq efrit-agent--todos nil)
  (setq efrit-agent--activities nil)
  (setq efrit-agent--pending-question nil)
  (setq efrit-agent--pending-tools (make-hash-table :test 'equal))
  (setq efrit-agent--streaming-message nil)
  (setq efrit-agent--thinking-indicator nil)
  (setq efrit-agent--todos-region nil)
  (setq efrit-agent--expansion-state (make-hash-table :test 'equal))
  ;; Ensure region markers still exist
  (unless (and efrit-agent--conversation-end
               (marker-position efrit-agent--conversation-end))
    (efrit-agent--init-regions)
    (efrit-agent--setup-regions))
  ;; Start/restart elapsed timer
  (when efrit-agent--elapsed-timer
    (cancel-timer efrit-agent--elapsed-timer))
  (setq efrit-agent--elapsed-timer
        (run-at-time 1 1 #'efrit-agent--update-elapsed (current-buffer)))
  ;; Insert visible delimiter between sessions
  (efrit-agent--append-to-conversation
   (propertize (format "\n══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Session: %s
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n"
                       (truncate-string-to-width command 50))
               'face 'efrit-agent-section-header
               'efrit-type 'session-delimiter)))
```

title: Design: Context budget management for expanded tool set
description:
With more tools gathering more context, we need smarter context management.

## Design Complete ✓

See: docs/design/context-budget-management.md

## Key Design Decisions

### 1. Token Estimation (not counting)
- Use character-based estimation (~3.5 chars/token)
- Accurate enough for budgeting (within 20%)
- Avoids tokenizer dependency

### 2. Budget Tiers
- System Prompt: 8k tokens
- Work History: 12k tokens (compressed)
- Tool Results: 40k tokens (current call)
- User Message: 10k tokens
- Response Buffer: 30k tokens
- **Total Target: 100k** (safe margin below 200k limit)

### 3. Two-Phase Result Delivery
- **Immediate**: Full result for Claude's use
- **Historical**: Compressed to ~500 chars for work log

### 4. Tool-Specific Compression
Each tool has custom compression for history:
- project_files: "500 files, types: .el (234), .md (45)..."
- search_content: "50 matches in 12 files: file1.el (5)..."
- read_file: "Read file.el (1234 lines). Key sections..."
- vcs_diff: "5 files, +234/-89 lines. Modified: ..."

### 5. Dynamic Budget Hints
Tool schemas update with remaining budget:
- "Current budget allows ~200 files"
- "[Budget Alert: ~20k tokens remaining]"

### 6. Pure Executor Compliance
- Efrit: counts, truncates, reports (mechanical)
- Claude: decides what's important, what to summarize, when to stop

## Implementation Phases

1. **Budget Tracking**: New efrit-budget.el with core structs
2. **Tool Updates**: Each tool respects budget parameter
3. **Session Integration**: Budget tracking in efrit-session.el
4. **Dynamic Schemas**: Budget hints in tool descriptions

## Next Steps

Create implementation issues from this design.

design:
## What to Build

```elisp
(defun efrit ()

For one-off commands without the REPL UI, use \\[efrit-do] instead."

        (goto-char efrit-agent--input-start)))))
```

title: Shell security: ssh/scp/rsync allowed by default - document remote host risk

title: End agent session properly on loop completion
description:
Signal session completion to the agent buffer when the async loop ends.

CURRENT STATE:
- efrit-agent-set-status exists and works with: working, paused, waiting, complete, failed
- No efrit-agent-end-session function exists yet
- efrit-do-async--stop-loop (line 319) handles session termination

IMPLEMENTATION:

APPROACH A (Recommended - Add public function):
1. In efrit-agent.el, add after efrit-agent-set-status (around line 811):
   (defun efrit-agent-end-session (success-p)
     "End the current agent session.
   SUCCESS-P determines whether to show complete or failed status."
     (efrit-agent-set-status (if success-p 'complete 'failed)))

2. In efrit-do-async--stop-loop (line 319), add after line 327:
   (efrit-agent-end-session (string= stop-reason "end_turn"))

APPROACH B (Use set-status directly):
1. In efrit-do-async--stop-loop, add after line 327:
   (efrit-agent-set-status
     (if (string= stop-reason "end_turn") 'complete 'failed))

CONTEXT - stop-reason values:
- "end_turn" = Claude finished successfully
- "interrupted" = User interrupted (C-g)
- "api-error" = API call failed
- "iteration-limit-exceeded" = Hit max iterations
- "session-complete" = Tool signaled completion
- "unknown-stop-reason" = Unexpected stop reason

All non-"end_turn" reasons should show 'failed status.

FILES: lisp/interfaces/efrit-agent.el, lisp/interfaces/efrit-do-async-loop.el
VERIFICATION: Run efrit-do to completion, verify agent buffer shows 'complete' status. Then interrupt with C-g, verify it shows 'failed'.

Bug: API errors don't display in agent buffer when regions uninitialized
description:
When an API call fails early (before agent buffer is properly initialized), the error handler efrit-agent--add-error-message crashes with:

'Wrong type argument: markerp, nil'

This happens because the function tries to use efrit-agent--conversation-end marker without checking if it exists first.

Root cause: API error callbacks can fire before the agent buffer has initialized its region markers.

Fixed: Added marker existence check at function start (same pattern used in efrit-agent--stream-start-message).

This was causing the log errors:
[20:53:20] ERROR: API request failed: Wrong type argument: markerp, nil

Add session persistence for agent buffer
description:
Save and restore agent buffer conversation when buffer is killed.

CURRENT STATE:
- efrit-transcript-save saves session to disk
- efrit-transcript-load loads session by ID
- efrit-transcript-list returns available transcripts
- efrit-agent-mode has kill-buffer-hook for cleanup (line 263)

IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Add save-on-kill in efrit-agent-core.el:
   - In kill-buffer-hook (already exists), call transcript save
   - Only save if session has content worth saving

2. Add restore option in efrit-agent-start-session (to be created in ef-33f):
   - Check if transcript exists for session-id
   - If exists, prompt: Restore previous session? y/n
   - If yes, load and replay messages to agent buffer

3. Key functions to use:
   (efrit-transcript-save session) - saves session
   (efrit-transcript-load session-id) - returns session struct or nil
   (efrit-session-conversation-history session) - gets messages

4. Restore flow:
   (let ((old-session (efrit-transcript-load session-id)))
     (when (and old-session (y-or-n-p "Restore previous session? "))
       (dolist (msg (efrit-session-conversation-history old-session))
         (let ((role (nth 0 msg)) (content (nth 1 msg)))
           (pcase role
             (user (efrit-agent--add-user-message content))
             (assistant (efrit-agent--add-claude-message content)))))))

FILES: lisp/interfaces/efrit-agent-core.el, lisp/core/efrit-session-transcript.el
VERIFICATION: Run efrit-do, let it complete, kill buffer, run efrit-agent, verify restore prompt appears.
